posts.title: Musk Chose Trump Over Ukraine, and the Starlink Cut Shows It
posts.dek: The Starlink restrictions on Ukraine look to me like politics, not a technical call.
posts.author: Daniel
posts.body:
## What happened

Ukraine's access to Starlink has been newly restricted, and Ukrainian officials say the limits are disrupting their drone operations against Russian targets [1][2]. A Zelensky adviser says access was restricted without notice, and that this "cannot be a coincidence" [2]. That claim comes from one side, and no explanation from the provider has been reported [2].

## Why it matters

Starlink is a weapon now. For the United States, it's leverage over who gets access. For Ukraine, it's make-or-break.

My read is that this points to collusion between Elon Musk and President Trump. I think Musk would rather back Ukraine, but crossing Trump costs him more, and Trump holds much of Starlink's future. Loyalty to Trump is his best shot at keeping Starlink and his other businesses thriving. I don't see much debate there. So he's bending the knee.

What sells it for me is the timing. Trump pressed Ukraine to stop hitting Russian refineries [2]. Right after that, Starlink was throttled. I can't see a universe where that's an accident.

Elon's rhetoric on X has turned against Zelensky too. To me, it reads like a concerted effort to go after him, with talk of elections and of getting him out of office [3].

{{M1}}

The reporting covers the restrictions, the damage Ukraine describes and the timing. That Musk did it for Trump is my interpretation.

## Where it's headed

I think this is a midterm play, and maybe a desperate one. They need unity and good news, and ending the war in Ukraine could move votes. With Ukraine's refinery strikes paused [2], markets could read that as a signal, and prices might fall.

Ukraine's access hangs on how the midterms go. I just don't expect things to get better once they're over.

If SpaceX or the Pentagon calls this a technical or security decision, I'd read that as cover. What would move me is a joint statement from Ukraine or NATO allies that balances the picture. Even then, it depends. I could be wrong.

Whatever the explanation, Ukraine is paying for it. Follow the money. Watch the timing.

posts.title: Trump Can't Pressure Putin, So He's Squeezing Ukraine
posts.dek: Trump says signing now would scare Russia off. My read is there's a bigger plan we aren't being shown.
posts.author: Daniel
posts.body:
## What happened

On October 18, Trump posted on Truth Social that signing "that document" now would drive Russia away from the bargaining table, and that he "can sign it later, or any time that I want!" [1] In the same post, he said Russia is doing "very little, if anything" to help Iran, and he wants to keep it that way [1]. He also blamed Zelenskyy's strikes on Russian diesel refineries, saying they are "seriously hurting the world diesel markets, including those in the United States." [1]

{{M1}}

## Why it matters

I think there's a plan between Trump and Putin behind the scenes. I don't have proof of collusion, and I'm not going to pretend I do. But the pieces point to a picture.

Here's one of those pieces, and it's my read, not settled fact. My understanding is that Trump signed the Graham sanctions bill, H.R. 5334, on September 18, 2026, and is choosing not to enforce it. His own post talks about signing "that document" later, which doesn't line up neatly with that. Either way, the coverage says Trump is waiving the Russia sanctions, and he says it's to keep Moscow at the table.

Why go this route? I think it's because Trump has no leverage over Putin. None. So he's applying maximum pressure where he can, on Zelenskyy and on Europe. Push the side that will listen, and hope they cave.

That has a cost. It's alienating the United States from its allies and undoing goodwill this country built over the last 100 years. Trust like that took generations to earn, and it doesn't come back fast.

## Where it's headed

What the plan actually is, time will tell. Something is going on, and I'm confident about that much. The details I can't tell you yet.

Politically, I think this is a disaster for Trump heading into the midterms. We'll see what damage control he can pull off. But to me this mostly looks like desperation. A president with real leverage doesn't need to lean this hard on his own friends.

Putin made a bad decision invading Ukraine, and Trump is bailing him out.

media.author: Donald J. Trump
media.text: My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table. Great progress is being made, and that includes current hostage negotiations! Signing that document at this time will do that, and I can sign it later, or any time that I want! Perhaps more importantly, Russia is doing very little, if anything, to help the Islamic Republic of Iran, compared to what they could be doing, and I want to keep it that way, and will, unless stupid people get in the way. Lastly, Zelenskyy is using Diesel Refineries in Russia as a target, knowing that these attacks are seriously hurting the world diesel markets, including those in the United States. Farmers, ranchers, and businesses of all kinds are suffering greatly from this, but Russia is, nevertheless, sending, at a low price, millions of barrels of diesel to the World. Zelenskyy doesn’t care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him, and that Crooked Joe Biden gave him in the past, he doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did. He could have made a better deal two years ago than he can now. His country is in shambles, a large portion of his land is lost, his oceans and seas are gone, and his male population is low, wounded, and/or dead. I WANT THIS WAR END! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP
media.caption: Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump) on Truth Social, 10/18/26, 10:36 PM
media.alt: A Truth Social post by Donald J. Trump explaining his stance on Russia, the Russia-Ukraine peace negotiations, and criticizing Zelenskyy.
